newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: FLOODS IN SLOVAKIA UNDER CONTROL ARMY SAYS.
newsitem.headline: FLOODS IN SLOVAKIA UNDER CONTROL ARMY SAYS.

text.p: Floods, which have already ravaged parts of Poland and the Czech Republic, are threatening to wreak havoc in Slovakia as well, though officials said the situation has not yet reached a critical point.

Heavy rains which began last weekend have swollen several Slovak rivers and streams to 100-year record levels mainly in the northwest of the country. But so far the reported damage is said to be limited and there has been no loss of life.

The most critical situation has been reported in the western Slovak spa town Piestany on the river Vah, where the army had to evacuate some 15,000 inhabitants, the official Slovak news agency TASR reported on Thursday.
The Vah, Slovakia's longest river, runs from the High Tatra mountains down to the Hungarian border in the south where it links up with the Danube.
"The situation on the Vah is bad and dangerous in some places, but I do not consider it as critical," TASR quoted Chief of General Staff Jozef Tuchyna as saying.
"We have had (the situation) under control since the beginning of high water... we have already solved the most serious moments," Tuchyna said.
So far one person was reported missing but was said to have attempted to canoe down the swollen Vah.
In Poland and the Czech Republic, days of torrential rain have killed at least 32 people and forced tens of thousands to flee their homes.
